title: Stanford Just Fixed LLM Repetition: The VCM Breakthrough

scenes.title: The Likelihood Trap
scenes.headline: Why LLMs Get Dumber in Long Chains
scenes.visual_directive: Pulsing red alert banner 'The Likelihood Trap'; exponential curve flattening into repetitive loop; glowing warning badges
scenes.spoken_script: Have you ever noticed that the longer you chat with an AI reasoning model, the more repetitive and generic it sounds? It's not your prompt—it's a fundamental flaw in modern language modeling known as the Likelihood Trap. As reasoning chains stretch to dozens of steps, models fall into predictable, dull vocabulary loops that standard sampling cannot escape.

scenes.title: Why Legacy Decoders Fail
scenes.headline: The Scale-Variance Flaw
scenes.visual_directive: Logit distribution bar graph with high variance spikes; animated X on fixed scalar penalties; breakdown of confident vs exploratory token states
scenes.spoken_script: Most developers try cranking up temperature or setting a fixed repetition penalty. But Stanford researchers discovered why that fails: logit variance changes dynamically at every single token! In confident states, a fixed penalty does nothing. In uncertain exploratory states, that same penalty destroys semantic coherence and breaks math proofs.

scenes.title: The VCM Architecture
scenes.headline: Variance-Calibrated Modulation (VCM)
scenes.visual_directive: Neon cyan architecture flow; formula callout M_t = Z_t - λ·Prior - γ·σ_t·Count; Contextual Searchlight beam illuminating keywords; σ_t standard deviation meter
scenes.spoken_script: To solve this, researchers introduced Variance-Calibrated Modulation, or VCM. It makes two key mathematical moves before decoding: First, a Contextual Searchlight using Pointwise Mutual Information subtracts unconditional prior logits, naturally extinguishing generic filler stopwords. Second, Adaptive Self-Debiasing scales the repetition penalty by the real-time standard deviation of the logits vector.

scenes.title: The Payoff & Implementation
scenes.headline: +38.4% Reasoning Diversity • 0ms Overhead
scenes.visual_directive: Rocketing benchmark comparison bars; +38.4% diversity metric; green verified checkmarks for vLLM and llama.cpp; final CTA card to Govind's blog
scenes.spoken_script: The payoff is massive: a thirty-eight percent boost in reasoning diversity, a ninety-five percent drop in repetitive degeneration, and zero extra inference latency. Even better, VCM is completely training-free—you can hook it directly into vLLM, Ollama, or llama.cpp in under thirty lines of code. Check out the full technical breakdown and implementation on the blog.
